summary: # CLO 2024 Academic Month: Practice of Curriculum Reform in Fashion Design Based on CLO3D ## Introduction I'm going to share with you how CLO3D is used in our clothing professional class system. My topic is how CLO3D is utilized in the reform of the clothing professional class system. This discussion is mainly divided into five aspects: 1. Introduction of our school and the rationale for this course and software. 2. Background of our professional class system reform. 3. Exploration of the reform in clothing professions, including clothing design and engineering. 4. Case studies showcasing how we use CLO3D in the course. 5. Next steps for further implementing the reform of the class system. ## Our School Our school is a public art institution focused primarily on design. The characteristics of our school emphasize public art and design. In our clothing department, we aim to align with our school's philosophy by emphasizing clothing innovation and implementation. We have integrated a series of classes involving traditional clothing culture, craftsmanship, patterns, cultural history, etc., into a specialized course module. The main focus of our training is on cultivating creative application design talent that encompasses science, humanities, art, and practical skills. The purpose of this introduction is to explain how we implement this talent goal in our courses. The class reform in the Department of Clothing began in 2017, driven by the digital transformation of the fashion industry. The direction of clothing development is increasingly toward intelligent, functional, and digital technologies. ## Historical Context During my time at Donghua University, we aimed to promote CLO3D starting in 2010, recognizing it as a potential future direction after attending a presentation about it. At that time, CLO3D was not yet widely developed in China. My personal experience and research focus on functional clothing and digital fashion have influenced my professional development. In 2016, we proposed the construction of a digital lab, and in 2019, with the support of CLO3D and local resources in Shanghai, we established our clothing digital lab. We introduced CLO3D software, a human-to-human scanning system, and a fabric scanning machine in 2020. By 2022, we completed human-to-human measurements, constructed 3D models, and began fabric-based production. However, we still need a system to test the physical performance of fabrics, as current scanning only provides shape and 3D modeling, leaving us searching for better processing methods. This challenge remains unsolved, and we plan to address it in the coming years. ## Reform of the Clothing Professional Class System Our clothing professional course system is undergoing significant reform. Initially, we transitioned from single courses to a comprehensive course system. ### Course Structure Development In 2020, I taught a course called Clothing Design Technology, which was one of the first to incorporate CLO3D after its introduction. This was initially a standalone course, but we gradually expanded its integration into multiple courses. Our software application has evolved from merely showcasing technology to integrating it into product development across various courses. Since last year, we have explored a fusion of CLO3D and Blender software, enhancing our curriculum. ### Human Development Program Our earliest courses centered around CLO3D technology, emphasizing traditional floating board structures. In 2022, we shifted focus to a more integrated approach to CLO3D, moving away from flat structures to three-dimensional representations. We introduced a course called Fuzhang Three-Dimensional Virtual Representation, which teaches students the fundamentals of CLO3D from basic to advanced levels. This course is offered in collaboration with the Department of Clothing and Human Resources Engineering, where students utilize CLO3D in their design projects. ## Case Studies ### Case 1: Clothing and Human Resources Engineering Course In our clothing and human resources engineering course, we begin with basic software training, covering garment types like shirts and trousers. In the latter part of the course, students expand their designs, applying structural design principles to showcase their work in three-dimensional forms. This foundational course is introduced in the first year to help students master software skills early. Previously, students had used Photoshop and Illustrator, but we encourage independent learning alongside structured classroom instruction. ### Case 2: Advanced Software Technology Course In another course, we focused on 3D human scanning methods, collecting data models from scans. Collaborating with our digital academy, we processed these models and learned how to create basic versions suitable for human body fitting. Students then select materials and use our fabric scanner to create 3D representations of their chosen fabrics, followed by physical parameter analysis. This course includes a digital costume production process, culminating in a virtual fashion show. ### Innovation and Competitions Students participate in innovation projects, creating designs that incorporate traditional craftsmanship and modern digital techniques. For instance, one notable project involved designing a children's dragonfly suit, integrating modern concept designs with traditional cultural elements. ## Future Directions Looking forward, we aim to enhance our curriculum by creating a resource library to improve teaching efficiency with 3D technology. ### Integration of Technologies We envision combining CLO3D with other digital software for virtual dynamic displays and scene integration. This approach may lead to a future where physical models are replaced by virtual representations. ### Emphasis on Artificial Intelligence Incorporating artificial intelligence into our design process is essential. AI can enhance design efficiency, especially for engineering students, who may lack traditional drawing skills. We aim to foster design thinking and methodologies, allowing students to learn independently while providing guidance on their learning journeys. In conclusion, our journey through curriculum reform in fashion design based on CLO3D is ongoing, and we are committed to embracing innovation and technology to enhance our educational offerings. Thank you for your attention.
